tickets.reason: An 11.3-hour watch upload gap with a 'sync failed' message occurred while the spouse confirmed the patient was well and physiology remained at baseline.
The watch had a 13.2-hour battery gap and is down to 9% battery on Day 0 with the charging cable still missing, while the patient is clinically stable.
A watch firmware update caused a persistent skin-temperature shift that disagrees with both the ring and oral thermometer in an asymptomatic patient.
A watch app update changed the HRV reporting measure and shifted values higher while all other vitals and clinical status remained unchanged.
Re-pairing the watch to a replacement phone caused duplicated minute records that artificially doubled daily step counts in a stable patient.
Re-pairing the ring to a new phone shifted its internal clock 5 hours ahead of the bed sensor and caregiver observations in a stable patient.
The brief watch battery gap on Day -3 was already resolved when the charging lead was found on Day -2, and the current presentation is a real clinical heart failure exacerbation.
A CGM app update truncated exported readings above 200 mg/dL, creating an ongoing device fault on top of true hyperglycemia confirmed by fingerstick glucometer.
The faulty charging cradle was already replaced on Day -2 with continuous, verified watch data over the last 48 hours.

A prolonged 52-hour data gap in a patient with moderate dementia living alone without in-person verification is handled under high-risk gap rules rather than as a device ticket, and charging was subsequently restored.
The watch upload issue was already resolved via manual re-pairing on Day 0, and the patient has a real acute febrile illness requiring clinical routing without a device ticket.
